definition: A fact or event that can be observed, especially one that is unusual or hard to explain.
example: The northern lights are a natural phenomenon caused by particles from the sun striking the atmosphere.
nuance: Unlike a mere event, a phenomenon is something observed and studied; use phenomena, not phenomenon, for more than one.
prompt: A science class watches water droplets form on the outside of a cold glass.
options: The teacher said condensation is a phenomenon that occurs when moist air meets a cold surface.
The students phenomenon the droplets with a magnifying glass.
Three different phenomenon appeared on the glass that afternoon.
The students called it a phenomenon even though nothing on the glass could be seen or measured.
reasons: Condensation is an observable natural occurrence, so the noun fits exactly.
The word is a noun naming an occurrence; it cannot serve as a verb for looking closely.
After a number like three, the plural phenomena is required, not the singular form.
The word names something perceived; an event no one can detect in any way does not qualify.

practice.prompt: Every evening, thousands of birds swirl together above a small town's bridge.

reasons: This confuses the noun with the adjective phenomenal; a noun cannot describe how impressive a view is.
The singular noun cannot take the plural verb are; more than one would be phenomena.
Something no one has ever witnessed cannot be an observed occurrence, so the claim contradicts itself.
A striking, repeated event that people observe and try to explain is exactly this kind of thing.
